questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go somewhere in Europe

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was okay easy, but I think in Italy you have to be patient and have faith in that the information will come but it will not necessarily be in good advance.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was very lost on my first day of school, and did not know where to go or where my classes where. But i asked some people, and they guided me towards the room. There was an Erasmus office but they were not open when i arrived.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite hard, but we were 4 people trying to find a place so that has something to do with it. I think it would be easier if you are two people, also because there are more apartments available with those number of rooms. But we looked on housing sites like housing anywhere and AirBnb and I think just with common sense and by being cautious you can find a nice place.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: if you can find a place near a metro! I dindn't live near a metro and it could be a hassle getting around, and it would just take extra time. But the metros do close around midnight - but during the day the metro is great.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We has to look at the catalogue and find courses, and then they would send an email with a link for registration so that part was easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not much, the email did explain quite a lot. If i had any doubts I reached out to a friend who had been on Erasmus in Milan last year (so use network if any doubt).

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: There was 1 class I couldn't take since it wasnt uploaded, but the rest was fine. So it's good to do some orientation in regards to if there are other courses you are interested in, in case that your course is not available that semester year.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have patience. It takes some time with the italien school system, but things will work out fine.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had 3 MA courses and only on BA course. The level on MA was totally fine and aligned with BA classes in Copenhagen so that was perfectly fine. At some points it was repetitive for what we discussed in Copenhagen in semester 1, but it's always good with recapping.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It's not as academic as in Copenhagen. In Milan it was very much more about learning to think and reflect and not as much about the right academic framework or style in papers. But it was teacher towards student - like in Cph.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Journalism, Media and Politics
Globalization, Social Justice and Human Rights
Languages of the media
Digital society

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed the Globalization, social justice and human rights one!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Uber at night because metro is closed, and night busses are fine but sometimes it's good to just take an uber late at night. There are also Limes which are great. I think you can live in Milano for not that much as it is cheaper to go out, but it's expensive to really research a city.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Going out was cheaper that i thought. Housing was expensive, but it is possible to find cheaper than 6500 DKK.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not participate in that, but im sure that they have something great. There was a language course online, but it overlapped with my courses.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not sure - I did not explore that really that much.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join a club of some sort! or a language course. Enjoy the city!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: take some trips around in Italy. It's really easy with train and especially from Milan to other places. Turin was really nice and Bologna of course.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy - when you accept that things are just moving more slowly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: You can join Erasmus events, or talk with the people in your class. Ask them about assignments and such.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The fact that things move slow, but not so much other stuff.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The lifestyle of appreciation of the nice things in life. They know how to live life. I enjoyed the culture around dinner and have it last a long time.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Go out and enjoy the city! that's the best way to integrate and have a good time. 
Learn some italian if you can and want - it's much easier to navigate and talk with people if you know some stuff. (just ordering and such) 
There is dog poop on the streets so beware.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Be open minded and enjoy your time there. Go to the markets, learn some italian. Go to the courses and actually engage in the teaching materials. 
Talk with the locals, and try something new. And travel a bit if you can.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I loved getting a new perspective of the world through my classes and the people i met. Also you just learn so much about yourself by living "on your own" in a new country. It's a great learning experience.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Could be lonely, and I was missing the people back home. But that's natural.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
